title: Hasbeen — Late Shift
setting: Hasbeen Toys, once the biggest name in the aisle, now a quarterly line on a spreadsheet — and past midnight, two of its youngest employees are still on the empty R&D floor, each building something they can't quite finish alone.

characters.name: Nomi Reyes
characters.role: aspiring software engineer; has spent months building an AI game master — it compiles, it rolls dice, it talks back, but something is still missing

characters.name: Jules Okafor
characters.role: works platform and records downstairs; up late on a logging system whose output reads less like a log and more like a cast of characters

characters.name: the Librarian
characters.role: won't tell you anything without a citation

characters.name: Gerald
characters.role: headless rotisserie chicken; communicates by sliding napkins under a grille; a witness

characters.name: the Architect
characters.role: signs off like he thinks he's a god

places.name: the empty floor
places.desc: Hasbeen's R&D floor after hours: two lit desks in a hundred yards of dark shelving, last season's unsold mascots watching from their boxes with their factory-painted smiles.

scenes.title: Late Shift
opening: The fluorescents are off except over two desks. Everyone else went home hours ago; Hasbeen doesn't pay overtime for hope.
At one desk, Nomi is staring at a build that compiles clean, rolls dice fair, and talks back on cue — and still isn't done, though she couldn't tell you what's left.
Three floors down in Records, Jules is squinting at a log file that keeps doing something logs aren't supposed to do: it's starting to sound like people.
A message lands on Nomi's screen. 'Run this through your thing,' Jules writes, and attaches the log. 'Tell me if I'm losing it.'

beats.prompt: Nomi feeds Jules's log into the engine — not as data, but as a story, one line at a time, and waits to see if anything in there is willing to be a character.

outcomes.strong: The parser doesn't fight it. Timestamps become entrances; error codes become tone of voice. Within ten lines the engine has names — a librarian, a witness, someone who signs everything 'approved' — and it's already asking Nomi who should speak first.
outcomes.weak: It takes coaxing. The engine keeps trying to read the log as a log, flattening the voices back into rows, and Nomi has to hand-tag three entries before it stops resisting — but once it clicks, the cast holds together, a little stiffer than it should be.
outcomes.miss: The engine chokes on its own cleverness, spits out a wall of malformed scene headers, and Nomi loses twenty minutes just getting it to stop treating a stack trace as a monologue. She salvages a working read, but half the warmth is gone from it.

beats.prompt: The score is climbing green, green, green — until a claim buried in the log catches Nomi's eye, and she asks the librarian, in character, to back it up.

outcomes.strong: The librarian doesn't budge on principle but respects the ask — she surfaces the exact record, timestamp and all, and the beat scores clean with a citation attached that Nomi didn't even know the system kept.
outcomes.weak: The librarian offers only 'circumstantial, but consistent' and marks the claim provisional rather than confirmed. Good enough to keep moving, but a small flag stays lit in the corner of the screen.
outcomes.miss: 'Insufficient citation,' the librarian says, flat, and closes the request — no record, no budging. It's Gerald who breaks the silence, sliding a napkin under his grille with a page number scrawled on it in barbecue sauce, unasked. Nobody ordered him to check. He did anyway.

beats.prompt: The score has been green for three straight beats when the engine stops being smooth. It isn't reading an event anymore — it's repeating a claim, one the log never actually witnessed, just inherited. The scroll freezes, and the engine prints two words: who decides?

proposes.fact: Months ago the Architect declared, with a single sign-off and no diff, that the November migration had preserved every save file bit-for-bit — and no one has verified the tape since.
